note: Mastering English Library dictionary. Definitions, examples and Arabic by Mastering English Library. Levels: CEFR-J Wordlist (Tono Lab, TUFS) and Octanove Vocabulary Profile (CC BY-SA 4.0). IPA: ipa-dict (MIT).

senses.def: to talk quickly and in a way that is hard to understand
ex: The baby babbled happily in her cot.
He babbled on about nothing.

senses.def: a very young child who cannot yet walk or talk
ex: The baby is sleeping.
She is going to have a baby in May.

senses.def: a person who looks after children while their parents are out
ex: We need a babysitter for Saturday night.
The babysitter put the kids to bed.

senses.def: to the place or state where someone or something was before
ex: I'll be back in ten minutes.
Please give the book back.

senses.def: the part of your body between your neck and your legs, behind you
ex: My back hurts.
He lay on his back.

senses.def: the part of something that is furthest from the front
ex: Write your name on the back of the page.
We sat at the back of the bus.

senses.def: at or near the rear of something
ex: He left through the back door.
Sit in the back seat.

senses.def: to give support to a person or plan
ex: Many people back the new plan.
The bank backed the project with money.

senses.def: to move backwards, or make a vehicle move backwards
ex: She backed the car out of the garage.

senses.def: the part of a picture or scene that is behind the main things
ex: There are mountains in the background of the photo.
I can hear music in the background.

senses.def: a person's family, education and experience
ex: She comes from a poor background.
What is your educational background?

senses.def: a bag that you carry on your back
ex: He put his books in his backpack.
She travelled with just a small backpack.

senses.def: an extra copy of computer files kept in case the original is lost
ex: Make a backup of your photos.
I lost the file because I had no backup.

senses.def: extra help or support that is available if needed
ex: The police called for backup.
Take a backup plan in case it rains.

senses.def: towards the back, or with the back first
ex: She took a step backward.
Try counting backward from ten.

senses.def: an area of land behind a house
ex: The children are playing in the backyard.
We have a small vegetable patch in our backyard.

senses.def: salted or smoked meat from a pig, often eaten in thin slices at breakfast
ex: He had eggs and bacon for breakfast.
The smell of bacon filled the kitchen.

senses.def: not good; unpleasant or of low quality
ex: I have some bad news.
The weather was bad all weekend.

senses.def: harmful or likely to cause damage
ex: Sugar is bad for your teeth.

senses.def: serious or severe
ex: She has a bad cold.

mistake.wrong: This food is bad for taste.
mistake.right: This food tastes bad.
mistake.note: Use the verb taste with bad, not a phrase like bad for taste.

senses.def: a small piece of metal or cloth worn to show who you are or what you support
ex: The police officer showed his badge.
Each student wore a name badge.

senses.def: in a way that is not good or not successful
ex: She sings badly.
The team played badly yesterday.

senses.def: to a serious or great degree
ex: He was badly hurt in the crash.
We badly need more time.

senses.def: the bags and cases that you take with you when you travel
ex: Please collect your baggage at the carousel.
Hand baggage must be small.

mistake.wrong: I have two baggages.
mistake.right: I have two bags / two pieces of baggage.
mistake.note: baggage is uncountable, so it has no plural; say a piece of baggage.

senses.def: a person who makes and sells bread and cakes
ex: The baker gets up at four every morning.
I bought a loaf from the baker.

senses.def: a place where bread and cakes are made or sold
ex: The bakery on our street opens at six.
We bought fresh rolls from the bakery.

senses.def: the ability to keep steady without falling
ex: He lost his balance and fell off the bike.
Cats have excellent balance.

senses.def: a fair mix of different things
ex: Try to find a balance between work and rest.

senses.def: the amount of money in a bank account
ex: Check your account balance online.

senses.def: to stay steady, or to put something so that it does not fall
ex: She balanced a book on her head.
He balanced on one leg.

senses.def: to give equal importance to different things
ex: Parents have to balance work and family life.

senses.def: having different parts in the right amounts
ex: A balanced diet includes fruit and vegetables.
The report gives a balanced view.

senses.def: having little or no hair on the head
ex: My grandfather is completely bald.
He started going bald at thirty.

senses.def: stated in a plain way, without extra detail
ex: He gave a bald statement of the facts.

senses.def: to lose the hair on your head (usually balding)
ex: He is balding at the front.
Many men start balding in their forties.

senses.def: a slow, romantic song, or a long poem that tells a story
ex: She sang a sad ballad.
The old ballad tells of a brave knight.

senses.def: a type of dance performed on stage, telling a story with music
ex: She has studied ballet since she was five.
We saw a ballet at the opera house.

senses.def: a secret vote, or the paper used to vote
ex: The workers held a ballot on the plan.
Each voter marks a ballot in private.

senses.def: an official order that forbids something
ex: There is a ban on smoking in restaurants.
The government lifted the ban.

senses.def: to officially say that something is not allowed
ex: The school banned mobile phones.
He was banned from driving for a year.

senses.def: a long piece of cloth wrapped around an injury
ex: The nurse put a bandage on his knee.
She wore a bandage around her wrist.

senses.def: a sudden loud noise
ex: The door closed with a bang.
We heard a loud bang outside.

senses.def: a hard hit on something
ex: He got a bang on the head.

senses.def: to hit something hard, making a loud noise
ex: She banged the door and left.
Someone was banging on the window.

senses.def: to send someone away from a place as a punishment
ex: The king banished him from the country.
The thief was banished from the village.

senses.def: to get rid of a feeling or thought
ex: She tried to banish her fears.

senses.def: the punishment of being sent away from a place
ex: The writer lived in banishment for ten years.
Banishment was a common punishment in the past.

senses.def: a person who has an important job in a bank
ex: His father is a banker in London.
The banker explained the loan to us.

senses.def: to make a person or company unable to pay what they owe
ex: The cost of the court case bankrupted the family.
The long strike nearly bankrupted the firm.

mistake.wrong: The company bankrupted.
mistake.right: The company went bankrupt.
mistake.note: As an adjective, bankrupt is used with go: go bankrupt.

senses.def: the state of being unable to pay your debts
ex: The company filed for bankruptcy.
Many small shops face bankruptcy.

senses.def: not covered by clothes or shoes
ex: The children ran on the beach in bare feet.
He had bare arms in the cold.

senses.def: empty or without the usual things
ex: The room was bare except for a bed.
The shelves were bare.

senses.def: to uncover something so it can be seen
ex: The dog bared its teeth.
He bared his chest to the sun.

senses.def: only just; almost not
ex: I could barely hear her.
He barely passed the exam.

mistake.wrong: I barely don't know him.
mistake.right: I barely know him.
mistake.note: barely already has a negative meaning, so do not add not.

senses.def: the short loud sound a dog makes
ex: We heard the bark of a dog.
The bark scared the thief away.

senses.def: the hard outer covering of a tree
ex: The bark of this tree is very rough.

senses.def: to make the short loud sound of a dog
ex: The dog barked at the postman.
Our neighbour's dog barks all night.

senses.def: a plant grown for its grain, used for food, drinks and animal feed
ex: Farmers grow barley in the north.
The soup contains vegetables and barley.

senses.def: a large farm building for storing crops or keeping animals
ex: The hay is stored in the barn.
Cows spend the winter in the barn.

senses.def: relating to a highly decorated style of art, building and music from the 17th and 18th centuries
ex: The church has a beautiful baroque ceiling.
She plays baroque music on the violin.

senses.def: a large round container with flat ends, used for liquids
ex: The wine is stored in wooden barrels.
The shop sells oil by the barrel.

senses.def: the long tube of a gun
ex: He looked down the barrel of the gun.

senses.def: unable to grow plants or crops
ex: The land was dry and barren.
Nothing grows in this barren desert.

senses.def: a fence or wall that stops people from going somewhere
ex: Police put up barriers around the building.
The river forms a natural barrier.

senses.def: something that makes it difficult for something to happen
ex: Language is a barrier for many migrants.
The cost is a barrier to education.

senses.def: a person who makes and serves drinks at a bar
ex: The bartender poured him a drink.
She works as a bartender at weekends.

senses.def: the bottom part of something, on which it stands
ex: The lamp has a heavy base.
We camped at the base of the mountain.

senses.def: a place from which a person or company works
ex: The company has its base in Dubai.
The army has a base near the border.

senses.def: the main part or ingredient of something
ex: Tomatoes are the base of this sauce.

senses.def: to use an idea or fact as the starting point for something
ex: The film is based on a true story.
We based our decision on the facts.

senses.def: to have a place as your main place to live or work
ex: She is based in Riyadh.

mistake.wrong: The film is based in a true story.
mistake.right: The film is based on a true story.
mistake.note: Use based on, not based in, for the source of an idea.

senses.def: a room or floor of a building that is below ground level
ex: The washing machine is in the basement.
They rent a flat in a basement.

senses.def: in the most important ways; used to give the main point
ex: Basically, we need more money.
It's basically a good idea.

senses.def: the reason for doing something or the facts it is built on
ex: On what basis did you choose her?
The plan has no basis in fact.

senses.def: the way something is done or arranged (on a regular basis)
ex: He visits us on a regular basis.

mistake.wrong: There are two basises for the idea.
mistake.right: There are two bases for the idea.
mistake.note: The plural of basis is bases, said /ˈbeɪsiːz/.

senses.def: to wash yourself or someone else, or to swim for pleasure
ex: She bathed the baby in warm water.
We bathed in the cool river.

senses.def: to wash a part of the body with water, usually to clean a wound
ex: The nurse bathed his injured knee.

senses.def: to hit someone or something hard again and again
ex: Waves battered the small boat.
He battered the door with his fists.

senses.def: a mixture of flour, eggs and milk used for making pancakes or covering food before frying
ex: Dip the fish in batter before frying it.
Pour the pancake batter into the pan.

senses.def: in baseball, the player who tries to hit the ball
ex: The batter hit the ball over the fence.

senses.def: old, damaged or in bad condition from being used a lot
ex: He drove a battered old car.
She carried a battered suitcase.

senses.def: a fight between armies in a war
ex: Thousands of soldiers died in the battle.
The battle lasted three days.

senses.def: a hard struggle to win or achieve something
ex: She won her battle against cancer.
It was a battle to find a job.

senses.def: a place where a battle is fought or was fought
ex: Visitors can walk across the old battlefield.
Soldiers lay wounded on the battlefield.

senses.def: a small decoration, especially a shiny ball hung on a Christmas tree
ex: The children hung red baubles on the tree.
She wore a cheap bauble on her wrist.

senses.def: a part of the coast where the land curves inwards
ex: The boats were anchored in the bay.
We swam in a quiet bay.

senses.def: an area of a building set aside for a particular purpose
ex: The lorry reversed into the loading bay.

senses.def: used to say what someone or something is, or where they are
ex: She is a doctor.
The keys are on the table.

senses.def: used with an -ing form or past participle to make verb forms
ex: They are sleeping.
The window was broken by a ball.

mistake.wrong: She is work in a bank.
mistake.right: She works in a bank.
mistake.note: Do not add is before another verb in the simple present; Arabic has no be-verb here.

senses.def: the hard pointed part of a bird's mouth
ex: The bird carried a worm in its beak.
The eagle has a sharp, curved beak.

senses.def: a line of light, or energy that travels in one direction
ex: A beam of light came through the window.
The torch has a powerful beam.

senses.def: a long, thick piece of wood or metal that supports a roof or floor
ex: The old house has wooden beams across the ceiling.

senses.def: the hair that grows on a man's chin and cheeks
ex: My uncle has a long grey beard.
He shaved off his beard.

senses.def: having a beard
ex: A tall bearded man opened the door.
The bearded fisherman smiled.

senses.def: a connection with, or effect on, something (bearing on)
ex: The weather has no bearing on our plan.
His past has a bearing on this case.

senses.def: a position or direction in relation to a place (usually plural)
ex: I lost my bearings in the dark forest.

senses.def: an animal, especially a large or dangerous one
ex: In the story, a terrible beast lives in the forest.
The farmer fed his beasts of burden.

senses.def: a person who is cruel or violent
ex: He was a beast to his workers.

senses.def: to win against someone in a game or competition
ex: Our team beat them three to one.
She beat me at chess.

senses.def: to hit someone or something hard and many times
ex: The rain beat against the window.
He was beaten by the thieves.

senses.def: to mix food quickly with a fork or whisk
ex: Beat the eggs and sugar together.

senses.def: a strong regular sound in music
ex: I love the beat of this song.
The drums kept a steady beat.

senses.def: one movement of the heart
ex: Her heartbeat was fast.

mistake.wrong: Our team won them.
mistake.right: Our team beat them.
mistake.note: Use beat with an opponent; win is used with the game or prize.

senses.def: very attractive or pleasing to look at, hear or experience
ex: She has a beautiful smile.
It's a beautiful day.

senses.def: in a very attractive or very skilful way
ex: She sings beautifully.
The room was beautifully decorated.

senses.def: the quality of being very attractive to look at
ex: We admired the beauty of the mountains.
She is a woman of great beauty.

senses.def: a beautiful person or thing
ex: That old car is a real beauty.

senses.def: a brown animal with a flat tail that builds dams across rivers
ex: The beaver built a dam across the stream.
Beavers cut down trees with their teeth.

senses.def: used to give the reason for something
ex: I stayed home because I was ill.
She is happy because it's her birthday.

mistake.wrong: Because I was tired. I went to bed.
mistake.right: Because I was tired, I went to bed.
mistake.note: A because clause cannot stand alone as a sentence; join it to the main clause.

senses.def: to start to be something or to change into something
ex: She became a doctor.
It is becoming colder.

mistake.wrong: He became to be angry.
mistake.right: He became angry.
mistake.note: become is followed directly by an adjective or noun, with no to be.

senses.def: a piece of furniture that you sleep on
ex: I made my bed this morning.
The children go to bed at eight.

senses.def: the bottom of a river, sea or area of garden
ex: There are flower beds along the path.

senses.def: the past participle of be, used with have to talk about experience or time up to now
ex: I have been to Paris twice.
She has been ill all week.

senses.def: used to say that someone has gone to a place and come back
ex: Have you ever been to London?

mistake.wrong: I have been in Dubai last year.
mistake.right: I was in Dubai last year.
mistake.note: Use the past simple, not the present perfect, with a finished time like last year.

senses.def: a bitter alcoholic drink made from grain
ex: He ordered a glass of beer.
Two beers, please.

senses.def: at an earlier time
ex: I have seen this film before.
She came the day before.

senses.def: earlier than a particular time or event
ex: Wash your hands before lunch.
We arrived before noon.

senses.def: earlier than the time when something happens
ex: Call me before you leave.
Think before you speak.

mistake.wrong: Before to leave, he locked the door.
mistake.right: Before leaving, he locked the door.
mistake.note: After before as a preposition, use the -ing form, not to + verb.

senses.def: before something else happens
ex: Please tell us beforehand if you cannot come.
I cooked the meal beforehand.

senses.def: to ask people for money or food because you are poor
ex: Some children were begging on the street.
He had to beg for food.

senses.def: to ask for something in an urgent or emotional way
ex: She begged him to stay.
I beg you to listen.

senses.def: the first part or start of something
ex: I read the book from beginning to end.
At the beginning of the year, I made a plan.

senses.def: used in on behalf of to mean acting for someone or something
ex: I am writing on behalf of the whole class.
She accepted the prize on behalf of the team.

senses.def: to act in a particular way
ex: He behaved badly at the party.
The children behaved very well.

senses.def: to be good, polite or well controlled (behave yourself)
ex: Please behave yourself in the restaurant.

senses.def: the way that a person or animal acts (American spelling)
ex: Her behavior in class was excellent.
Scientists study animal behavior.

mistake.wrong: The children's behaviors are good.
mistake.right: The children's behaviour is good.
mistake.note: behaviour is usually uncountable, so it is used with a singular verb.

senses.def: an order or request, usually in at someone's behest (formal)
ex: He came at the behest of the king.
She resigned at the behest of her employer.

senses.def: at the back of someone or something
ex: She looked behind and saw a dog.
He left his umbrella behind.

senses.def: later than planned or others
ex: I am behind with my homework.

senses.def: at the back of someone or something
ex: The cat is behind the sofa.
He hid behind a tree.

senses.def: supporting a person or plan
ex: The whole team is behind you.

senses.def: a living person or creature
ex: Humans are social beings.
They believe strange beings live on that planet.

senses.def: the state of existing (come into being)
ex: The company came into being in 1990.

senses.def: a strong feeling that something is true or exists
ex: She has a strong belief in honesty.
It is my belief that he is innocent.

senses.def: a religious or political idea
ex: People of all beliefs live here.

senses.def: to think that something is true or that someone is telling the truth
ex: I don't believe you.
Do you believe his story?

senses.def: to have an opinion that something is likely
ex: Police believe the thief is still in town.

senses.def: to feel that something exists or is good (believe in)
ex: Do you believe in ghosts?
I believe in working hard.

mistake.wrong: I believe to him.
mistake.right: I believe him.
mistake.note: Use believe someone to accept what they say, and believe in someone to trust them.

senses.def: angry and ready to fight or argue
ex: The drunk man became belligerent.
He spoke in a belligerent tone.

senses.def: to be owned by someone
ex: This bag belongs to me.
Who does this book belong to?

senses.def: to be a member of a group or club
ex: She belongs to a chess club.

senses.def: to have a proper place
ex: The plates belong in that cupboard.

mistake.wrong: This book is belonging to me.
mistake.right: This book belongs to me.
mistake.note: belong is not used in the continuous form and needs to.

senses.def: the things that you own, especially things that you can carry
ex: Please take all your belongings with you.
She packed her belongings into two bags.

senses.def: loved very much
ex: She cried at the loss of her beloved husband.
The city is beloved by tourists.

senses.def: a strip of leather or cloth worn around the waist
ex: He wore a black leather belt.
Tighten your belt.

senses.def: a loop of material that moves parts of a machine
ex: The belt on the engine broke.

senses.def: a strap that keeps you safe in a car or plane (seat belt)
ex: Always fasten your seat belt.

senses.def: in a lower position than something; under
ex: The cat slept beneath the table.
The sun sank beneath the horizon.

senses.def: hidden by the surface of something
ex: There is a kind heart beneath his rough manner.

senses.def: having a good effect; helpful
ex: Exercise is beneficial to your health.
The change was beneficial for everyone.

senses.def: a person who receives money or another benefit, especially from a will
ex: She is the main beneficiary of her uncle's will.
Schools were the biggest beneficiaries of the new fund.

senses.def: a helpful or good effect, or something that helps you
ex: Exercise has many benefits.
The new road will be of benefit to everyone.

senses.def: money or help given by the government or an employer
ex: He receives unemployment benefit.
The job offers good benefits.

senses.def: to gain something good, or to help someone
ex: Students benefit from small classes.
The new law will benefit workers.

mistake.wrong: We benefited of the training.
mistake.right: We benefited from the training.
mistake.note: Use benefit from, not benefit of.

senses.def: not dangerous; used especially about an illness or tumour
ex: The doctor said the lump was benign.
It was a benign form of the disease.

senses.def: kind and gentle
ex: The old man gave her a benign smile.

senses.def: not straight; curved or twisted
ex: The metal bar was bent.
He walked with a bent back.

senses.def: to officially give money or things to someone after you die
ex: She bequeathed her house to her niece.
He bequeathed his books to the library.

senses.def: deprived of something or someone, especially after a loss
ex: He was bereft of hope.
The village was bereft of its young people.

senses.def: a small, round, juicy fruit without a stone
ex: We picked berries in the forest.
Birds eat the red berries.

senses.def: also; used to add another point
senses.ar: فضلاً عن ذلك؛ إضافةً إلى ذلك
ex: I don't want to go; besides, it's late.
He plays tennis and golf, and swims besides.

senses.def: in addition to; as well as
ex: Besides English, she speaks German.
Who came besides you?

mistake.wrong: Besides the river, there is a park.
mistake.right: Beside the river, there is a park.
mistake.note: beside means next to, but besides means in addition to.

senses.def: the most good; better than all others
ex: She is my best friend.
This is the best pizza in town.

senses.def: in the way that is most good or most suitable
ex: I work best in the morning.
Which colour do you like best?

senses.def: to risk money on the result of a race, game or other event
ex: He bet ten pounds on the horse.
They bet on every match.

senses.def: used to say you are very sure about something (I bet)
ex: I bet she forgot the keys.

senses.def: to hurt someone who trusts you by not being loyal or honest
ex: He betrayed his best friend.
She felt betrayed by her family.

senses.def: to show a feeling that you want to hide
ex: Her voice betrayed her fear.

senses.def: of higher quality, or more suitable, than something else
ex: This phone is better than my old one.
I hope you get better soon.

senses.def: less ill than before
ex: I feel better today.

senses.def: in a more successful or more suitable way
ex: She speaks English better than me.
You'd better take an umbrella.

mistake.wrong: He is more better than me.
mistake.right: He is better than me.
mistake.note: better is already a comparative, so do not add more.

senses.def: in the space or time separating two things or people
ex: The shop is between the bank and the post office.
We eat nothing between lunch and dinner.

senses.def: shared by two or more people or things
ex: Divide the sweets between the children.

mistake.wrong: The difference between English and Arabic and French is big.
mistake.right: The difference between English and Arabic is big.
mistake.note: between is used with two things, and among with more than two.

senses.def: on the far side of; further than
ex: The village is beyond the hills.
Beyond the river is open farmland.

senses.def: more than a particular limit, or outside someone's ability
ex: The work is beyond my ability.
The damage was beyond repair.

senses.def: to offer a price for something you want to buy, especially at an auction
ex: He bid fifty pounds for the painting.
Three people bid for the old chair.

senses.def: to try to win a contract by offering to do work for a price
ex: Several firms are bidding for the contract.

senses.def: the act of offering prices at an auction
ex: The bidding started at one hundred pounds.
Bidding for the vase was fierce.

senses.def: orders that you obey (do someone's bidding)
ex: The servants did their master's bidding.

senses.def: large in size or amount
ex: They live in a big house.
He has a big family.

senses.def: important or serious
ex: Today is a big day for us.
She made a big mistake.

senses.def: a two-piece swimsuit worn by women
ex: She packed a bikini for the beach.
The shop sells bikinis in bright colours.

senses.def: a piece of paper that shows how much you must pay
ex: Can we have the bill, please?
The phone bill is very high.

senses.def: a piece of paper money (American English)
ex: He gave me a ten-dollar bill.

senses.def: a plan for a new law, discussed by a government
ex: Parliament passed the bill last night.

senses.def: to send someone a bill for goods or services
ex: The company will bill you monthly.
The hotel billed us for the extra night.

senses.def: a game played on a table with long sticks and balls
ex: They played billiards after dinner.
The club has a billiards room.

senses.def: the number 1,000,000,000; a thousand million
ex: The company is worth two billion dollars.
Billions of people use the internet.

mistake.wrong: There are three billions people.
mistake.right: There are three billion people.
mistake.note: After a number, billion has no -s, but billions of takes -s.

senses.def: a container for rubbish (British English)
ex: Put the paper in the bin.
The bin men come on Tuesday.

senses.def: to tie something tightly with rope or string
ex: They bound his hands with rope.
She bound the flowers with string.

senses.def: to force someone to follow a rule or promise
ex: The contract binds both sides.

senses.def: a short description of a person's life and work (short for biography)
ex: Read her bio on the website.
Write a short bio of yourself.

senses.def: relating to biology or to the natural processes of living things
ex: Eating is a biological need.
The experiment studied biological changes in plants.

senses.def: related by birth, not by adoption
ex: He met his biological mother at 30.

senses.def: the scientific study of living things
ex: She is studying biology at university.
I have a biology exam tomorrow.

senses.def: a senior priest in charge of churches in a large area
ex: The bishop spoke at the cathedral.
He was made a bishop last year.

senses.def: a chess piece that moves diagonally
ex: He moved his bishop across the board.

senses.def: a small piece or amount of something
ex: Would you like a bit of cake?
I'm a bit tired.

senses.def: the smallest unit of information in a computer
ex: A byte contains eight bits.

senses.def: growing or developing quickly
ex: The city has a burgeoning tech industry.
There is a burgeoning demand for solar power.

senses.def: a person who goes into a building to steal things
ex: A burglar broke into the shop at night.
The burglar alarm woke the neighbours.

senses.def: the crime of entering a building illegally to steal things
ex: There were three burglaries on our street last month.
He was arrested for burglary.

senses.def: the act of putting a dead body into the ground
ex: The burial took place on Friday.
They chose a quiet burial place.

senses.def: an injury to the skin caused by fire, heat or hot liquid
ex: She had a bad burn on her hand.
Put cold water on the burn.

senses.def: to destroy or damage something with fire, or to be on fire
ex: The old house burned to the ground.
He burnt the toast again.

senses.def: to hurt yourself with heat or fire
ex: Be careful or you'll burn your fingers.

senses.def: on fire, or feeling extremely hot
ex: Firefighters rushed into the burning building.
I felt a burning pain in my throat.

senses.def: very strong or urgent
ex: It was a burning issue for voters.

senses.def: to break open suddenly, or to make something break open, so that what is inside comes out
ex: The balloon burst with a loud bang.
The pipe burst and flooded the kitchen.

senses.def: to move or do something suddenly
ex: She burst into tears.
He burst into the room without knocking.

senses.def: a short period of sudden activity or noise
ex: There was a burst of applause.

senses.def: to put something or someone under the ground
ex: The dog buried a bone in the garden.
They buried him next to his wife.

senses.def: to cover or hide something completely
ex: The village was buried under snow.
She buried her face in her hands.

senses.def: the work of buying and selling goods or services
ex: He is in the clothing business.
Business is good this year.

senses.def: a company or shop that sells goods or services
ex: She runs a small business from home.

senses.def: something that concerns you personally
ex: What I do is not your business.

senses.def: to break something (informal)
ex: The kids busted the window with a ball.

senses.def: to arrest someone (informal)
ex: The police busted the gang last night.

senses.def: used to introduce an idea that is different from or opposite to what you have just said
ex: I like tea, but I don't like coffee.
He was tired but happy.

senses.def: except; apart from
ex: Everyone but Tom came to the meeting.
There was nothing to eat but bread.

senses.def: a person who cuts up and sells meat
ex: I bought lamb from the butcher.
The butcher's shop opens at eight.

senses.def: to kill an animal for meat, or to kill people in a cruel way
ex: The farmer butchered two pigs for the winter.

senses.def: to get something by paying money for it
ex: I want to buy a new phone.
She bought her son a bike.

mistake.wrong: I bought it from 50 dollars.
mistake.right: I bought it for 50 dollars.
mistake.note: Use for before the price you pay, not from.

senses.def: a person who buys something, especially something expensive
ex: The house has finally found a buyer.
Buyers are looking for cheaper cars.

senses.def: a continuous low sound like a bee makes
ex: I heard the buzz of a fly near the window.
A buzz of voices came from the room.

senses.def: a feeling of excitement or great interest
ex: There is a lot of buzz about the new film.

senses.def: to make a continuous low sound like a bee
ex: Flies buzzed around the food.
The phone buzzed on the table.

senses.def: a large bird of prey that hunts small animals
senses.ar: صقر أحمر الذيل؛ نوع من الصقور
ex: A buzzard circled above the field.

senses.def: an electrical device that makes a buzzing sound as a signal
ex: Press the buzzer if you know the answer.
The buzzer on the door rang twice.

senses.def: used to show who or what does or makes something
ex: The book was written by a teacher.
The window was broken by the wind.

senses.def: used to show the way something is done
ex: I go to work by bus.
You can pay by card.

senses.def: next to or very near someone or something
ex: She sat by the window.

senses.def: not later than a particular time
ex: Please finish it by Friday.

mistake.wrong: I go to school with bus.
mistake.right: I go to school by bus.
mistake.note: Use by (not with) before a means of transport: by bus, by car, by train.

senses.def: used when you leave someone or end a phone call; short for goodbye
ex: Bye, see you tomorrow!
She waved and said bye.

senses.def: to avoid a rule or a person by finding another way
ex: The company bypassed the usual approval process.
He bypassed his manager and spoke to the director.

senses.def: to go around a place instead of through it
ex: The new road bypasses the town centre.
